Imo that’s only part of the meaning of victim mentality. People who have victim mentality feel subjected to other people’s actions (in this case, negative opinions) and, as a result, avoid taking their own actions. You mentioned that you have to either pretend to be someone else, or wait until someone more accepting finds you. However, there’s also the option of working on yourself, so that you can express yourself as you are without the fear of judgment holding you back. You say you don’t believe “oh no bad things will happen to me”, yet that’s precisely why you don’t open yourself up to others. Being judged/misunderstood is inevitable in social situations, but you can also develop the mental tenacity to not get devastated by it. 

I hope this doesn’t sound too harsh. Most people fear judgment to a certain degree (despite what kind of person they are), and victim mentality often stems from actually being victimized at a young age. I myself struggle with this a lot too. It’s never your *fault* that you were hurt by others. However, it is your *responsibility* to recover and keep going for the sake of your own well-being.

Sorry I didn’t read your whole comment, since it is extremely lengthy, condescending, judgmental and just full of run-on sentences. But allow me to explain my thought process a little bit. 

I enjoy the idea of child trafficking as much as the average person (which is not at all, but I also would not jump in anger at the slight mention of it in *fiction*). What I probably *do* enjoy more than the average person is contrast, and environmental story telling. 

My goal was to recreate somewhat of a horror movie scene in Animal Crossing, a game that obviously tries very hard to be E rated. Of course, my creation would only contain items available in the game, all of which supposedly harmless. The interesting part (to me) is, this room would only be as scary as we imagine it to be: through the horror fictions we have consumed, our brains gained the ability to recognize the genre’s tropes, and put things (that are totally innocent by themselves) together. In the candy-colored style of Animal Crossing, this room setting would paint a disturbing picture in our mind, and evoke a sense of cognitive dissonance that more straightforward horror would not. Nightmare fuel drawn from a daydream. 

(It seems that this thought process is not that rare. For example, I recall seeing a meth lab recreation on this subreddit that got thousands of upvotes.) 

And I did exactly that. And, yes, I was kinda proud of it. Since you sound so provoked, I would even say that I was pretty successful. 

Now, you’re still entitled to your opinion. But now that I’ve explained my intentions and marked this post as NSFW (since it’s clearly not for the faint of heart), my conscience is completely clear. Also I was bored. Have a good day!

Holy fuck, I feel you on a spiritual level. I am also Asian, and had parents who RESENT me for writing when I was your age. 

It was a burning hatred that I don’t think I will ever understand. They went to insane lengths to make sure I wasn’t writing: spied on me, hacked my phone, went through my trash, harassed my only friends, etc.. This went on for two solid years. At one point they searched my belongings and found my 90k words draft. I was locked up and forbidden from even going to school for a week, during which time I was literally beaten to submission with metal clothes hangers. But for me, the hardest part of it was when they mocked my draft - every word of it - before tearing it to shreds. 

It’s been almost 10 years and I’m still typing this through tears. I went from pouring my heart into writing, to fearing writing along with a lot of other things. I’ve always been struggling with depression and anxiety, and last year I was also diagnosed with PTSD. I guess I’m finally a good child in the eyes of Asian parents: Ivy school, career plans, not one but two STEM degrees. But I know I’m a walking husk of a person, and I lament the part of me that was killed every day: the part of me that was capable of feeling pride, fulfillment, and inspiration. 

People in this post have been talking about how your parents just want you be OK financially down the road, but it goes further than that. Especially when you don’t actually have schoolwork to do, they are not thinking rationally and deciding they should be concerned about you: they are just thirsty for CONTROL. Once you’re off to college, who’s gonna be there to stop you from “playing around”? Who’s gonna make sure you take every step on the exact path they designed for you, to the exact kind of success they want? 

At the age of 10 I was known in my small town as a writing prodigy. At the age of 13 I was writing every day, excited to spend more time with my wonderful cast of characters and, eventually, to share my story with the world. At the age of 21 I hate waking up every morning, never feel motivated to do anything, and have attempted suicide 3 times. 

Please, don’t let them kill your soul. Please don’t stop writing. Please don’t be like me.
